sentences.text: This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 21.12.2018.

2. The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 21.12.2018 at about 4.25 a.m., the petitioner was waiting at the bus stop of M S Palya for boarding the bus to travel to Bangalore bus stop.
At that time, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.53.F.257 came from Laxmipura side and stopped the bus.

At which point of time, petitioner was for to board to the Bus through steps of the bus doors, at that time, the driver of the said Bus driven the same in a rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was aged about 23 years, he was working as a Engineer at Intellett Company and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to injuries sustained by him, he was not able to attend his work for a period of 3 months and lost his income during the said period.
The accident in question was occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.53.F.257.
Hence, the respondent is solely liable to pay the compensation.

With these averments petitioner prayed to award compensation..
3.
In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

4. The written statement averments of the respondent are hereunder:
The respondent has denied the cause and manner of accident and submitted that, the BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.53.F.257 was on its scheduled trip from Madhugirihalli Bus Stop to K R Market bus stop and when it reached M S Palya bus stop, the driver of the said bus after alighting the passengers and closing the doors, moved the bus slowly, at that time the petitioner ran to board the moving bus hurriedly and negligently.
Due to which, petitioner has lost control and fell on the road and sustained injuries.
Further contended that, there is a delay in lodging the complaint.
Further it has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Hence prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing No. KA.53.F.257 by its driver as contended in the petition ?

Therefore it is crystal clear that the petitioner has to prove his case based on the principle of preponderance of probabilities.
10. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries while boarding to the Bus through the steps.
At which point of time the driver of Bus driven the bus in a rash or negligent manner.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.

11.

According to respondent, on the date of alleged accident, the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.53.F.257 was drove the same slowly and cautiously and when the bus reached M S Palya bus stop, the driver of the said bus after alighting the passengers and closing the doors, moved the bus slowly, at that time the petitioner ran to board the moving bus hurriedly and negligently.
As such, the petitioner himself was wholly and solely responsible, but either the driver or the conductor of the bus was no way responsible.
12. In order to prove its contention, respondent has examined the driver of the offending Bus namely Srinivasaiah M V as R.W.1.
R.W.1 has filed affidavit by way of examination-in-chief.
R.W.1 has deposed that, he is the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.53.F.257 at the time of accident.
R.W.1 has reiterated the written statement averments of the respondent.
R.W.1 has been cross-
examined from the side of petitioner.
During the course of cross-examination, R.W.1 has admitted that, charge sheet has been filed against him and he has not challenged the charge sheet.
13. To prove the alleged negligence on the part of the petitioner, respondent has cross-examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only due to his negligence.
Except the driver of Bus, the respondent has not examined any eye witness to the accident.
Further, respondent has not produced any documents to show that, the accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, respondent has not placed positive evidence.
14. The other contention of the respondents is that, there are 71 days delay in lodging the complaint and the petitioner has not explained the reasons for the said delay.

Apart from that during the course of cross-examination of PW.1, he has deposed that he was not in a position to lodge the complaint.

In the instant case there is no dispute regarding while the petitioner was about to board the bus the accident took place.
Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, there is no malafide intention in lodging complaint after 71 days of the accident and the reasons assigned for delayed complaint is probable.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kusuma Latha Vs.
Satbir reported in 2011 (3) SCC 646, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, "the motor vehicles act is a beneficial legislation and that the claims under it must be decided on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities, not proof beyond reasonable doubt''.

Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in 2011 (4) SCC 693, between Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana and Others, wherein it is held that:
"It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case. Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot except a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim".

Further the Hon'ble Apex Court held that: "In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with the closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

20. ISSUE No.2:-
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent driving of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No. KA.53.F.257.
It is needless to mention that,
respondent

21. Age:- According to the petitioner, he was aged about 23 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Therefore in the absence of documents, on perusal of police and medical documents the age of the petitioner is shown as 23 years and hence the same is taken as the age of the petitioner.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 23 years.
Accordingly the age of the petitioner is considered as 23 years.
22. Income:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was working as an Engineer at INTELLETT Company and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate his income the petitioner has produced letter of appointment marked at Ex.P10, statement of account for the month of October 2017 to August 2019 marked at Ex.P19.
It is relevant to note that though petitioner has produced Ex.P10 and Ex.P19 he has not examined the employer.
Hence, this tribunal is declined to accept Ex.P10 & Ex.P19 and those documents will not come to the aid of petitioner to consider his income.

That apart, the Hon'ble High Court in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

24. In the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2018 is Rs.12,500/- per month.
In the instant case the accident occurred on 21.12.2018.
Hence the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.12,500/- per month.
25. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained grievous injuries.
He has produced wound certificate and discharge summary, which have marked as Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.12.
On perusal of Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.12, it reveals that, the petitioner has sustained compound grade I comminuted displaced spiral oblique fracture of distal 3rd both bone right leg.

It is relevant to mention that, respondent has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
26.
The petitioner has examined the witness namely Dr. B Ramesh, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria hospital as PW.2 and Medical Record Manager at MIOT International hospital as PW.3.

P.W.2 & 3 have filed affidavit by way of examination-in-chief and produced documents at Ex.P22 to Ex.P26.
27.
In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr. B Ramesh, Orthopedic Surgeon, Victoria hospital, Bengaluru as P.W.2.
This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of evidence and stated that, on 20.10.2022 petitioner came to their hospital for the assessment of disability.

Further deposed that, petitioner has sustained compound grade I comminuted displaced spiral oblique fracture of distal 3rd both bones of right leg and petitioner has also underwent operations for internal fixation of right tibia.

Further deposed that, on examination,
the petitioner now complains of pain in right leg, difficulty to squat on floor, climb upstairs, walk on slope, kneel stand on affected limb and difficulty to do routine activities.
Finally P.W.2 has stated that, petitioner has sustained 28% of disability to the right lower limb and 14% to the whole body.

sentences.text: P.W.2 has produced 2 documents, which have been marked as Ex.P.22 and Ex.P.23.
Ex.P.22 is the OP card and Ex.P.23 is the X-ray film.
He was cross-examined from the side of respondent at length.
During the course of cross- examination, he has deposed that, he is not the treated doctor.
Further deposed that, the petitioner can do his work by sitting in the office.
Further deposed that as per recent X-ray the wounds are healing and fractures are united.

28. On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness coupled with wound certificate clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury and suffered physical disability.
Further as per the admission of PW.2, the fractures have been united.
Hence by considering the avocation of petitioner, his age and injuries, the physical disability assessed by the P.W.2 is on higher side.
Hence, this Tribunal is considered the functional disability of the petitioner as 7% to the whole body.
29. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 23 years and his income is considered as Rs.12,500/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs. 1,50,000/- (12,500 x 12).

Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 18.
30.
If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,50,000 X 18), then it comes to Rs.27,00,000/-.
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 7% to the whole body.
The same amount of Rs.1,89,000/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disability.
31. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred some amount towards medical expenses, transportation, food and conveyance.

In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced 23 medical bills which have marked as Ex.P.17 for Rs.43,885/-, Ex.P21 for Rs.2,500/- and Ex.P33 for Rs.18,743/- and 8 medical prescriptions, which have been marked as Ex.P.18.
After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.65,128/- towards medical expenses.
32. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, due to accidental injuries, he has sustained permanent disability and he could not resume his avocation.

Further P.W.1 has stated that, he took treatment as an inpatient at MIOT International hospital from 21.12.2018 to 22.12.2018 and again from 24.04.2019 to 02.05.2019 and has sustained compound grade I comminuted displaced spiral oblique fracture of distal 3rd both bone right leg and has undergone surgery for closed intramedullary nailing right tibia with proximal and distal interlocking screws.
As per medical records and evidence of P.W.2 coupled with Ex.P.12 & 14, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for the period of 12 days.
Further as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical disability.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for 12 days.
As such, the petitioner has suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.

Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal award compensation of Rs.60,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

33. Loss of income during the laidup period:-

On perusal of these document, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 12 days.
Petitioner in his examination in chief has stated that he availed three months earned leave for the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident and has lost his income during that period.

However,
the petitioner has not produced document to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast two months rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was working as an Engineer at INTELLETT Company and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
This Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.12,500/- per month.
Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
34. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatinet for about 12 days.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of Food, Nourishment,
transportation and Atttendant charges.
35. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 23 years at the time of accident.
The disability and physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
36. Future medical expenses:- P.W.2, the medical witness deposed that, the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants.
Hence, by considering the future treatment and evidence of P.W.2, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 20,000/- towards future medical expenses.
37. Travel bills:
The petitioner has produced the travel bills marked at Ex.P34.
On perusal of these documents it appears to this tribunal that those receipts have been allegedly issued by the driver.
Moreover, the author of the bills have not been examined.
Hence Ex.P34 will not come to the aid of petitioner.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this head.
